content.test_md_blob:
# Complete guest checkout on a phone with a valid weekday delivery date

> Prove that a visitor can complete the end-to-end bouquet checkout as a guest on a phone-sized web surface, choose a non-Sunday delivery date, and reach an order confirmation that includes an order number.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a phone-sized browser viewport and land on the Bloom & Vine storefront home page.

## Step 2

From the bouquet catalogue, choose an in-stock bouquet that shows a visible price and add it to the basket.

## Step 3

From the basket, open checkout and continue without signing in or creating an account.

## Step 4

In the guest checkout form, enter {{guest_name}}, {{guest_email}}, {{guest_phone}}, and delivery address {{delivery_address}}.

## Step 5

In the delivery-date field, choose the non-Sunday date {{non_sunday_delivery_date}}.

## Step 6

In the payment section, use the approved test payment method {{payment_details}} and submit the order.

## Step 7

Assert the post-purchase page shows an order confirmation with a visible order number.

## Step 8 — assert @verifies ac-1, ac-2, ac-3, ac-6

Confirm presence check: order number on the order confirmation after a successful order (exists) — the stated promise: A successful order confirmation includes an order number.

content.title: Sunday delivery date is unavailable during guest checkout on a phone
content.test_md_blob:
# Sunday delivery date is unavailable during guest checkout on a phone

> Prove that the delivery-date control in the phone-sized guest checkout flow forbids selecting a Sunday.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a phone-sized browser viewport and land on the Bloom & Vine storefront home page.

## Step 2

From the bouquet catalogue, choose an in-stock bouquet that shows a visible price and add it to the basket.

## Step 3

From the basket, open checkout and continue without signing in or creating an account.

## Step 4

In the guest checkout form, enter {{guest_name}}, {{guest_email}}, {{guest_phone}}, and delivery address {{delivery_address}} up to the delivery-date field.

## Step 5

In the delivery-date picker, attempt to choose the Sunday date {{sunday_delivery_date}}.

## Step 6

Assert the Sunday date {{sunday_delivery_date}} remains unavailable for delivery selection.

## Step 7 — assert @verifies ac-5

Confirm 'a selectable Sunday delivery date' does NOT appear (forbidden-presence) — the stated promise: Delivery date selection does not allow Sundays.

objectives:
  - objective: Open {{start_url}} in a phone-sized browser viewport and land on the Bloom & Vine storefront home page.
    step: 1
  - objective: From the bouquet catalogue, choose an in-stock bouquet that shows a visible price and add it to the basket.
    step: 2
  - objective: From the basket, open checkout and continue without signing in or creating an account.
    step: 3
  - objective: In the guest checkout form, enter {{guest_name}}, {{guest_email}}, {{guest_phone}}, and delivery address {{delivery_address}} up to the delivery-date field.
    step: 4
  - objective: In the delivery-date picker, attempt to choose the Sunday date {{sunday_delivery_date}}.
    step: 5
  - objective: Assert the Sunday date {{sunday_delivery_date}} remains unavailable for delivery selection.
    step: 6
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: forbidden-presence
      operand: a selectable Sunday delivery date
      operator: exists
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-5
    objective: 'Confirm ''a selectable Sunday delivery date'' does NOT appear (forbidden-presence) — the stated promise: Delivery date selection does not allow Sundays.'
    step: 7

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Kept first because it automated the highest-value scenario: the full order-capture path on the source-required phone-sized surface.
[value_score] Kept second because it automated the only distinct negative outcome explicitly promised by the source: Sunday must not be selectable.

[self_critique] The check was narrowed to the visible order number on the confirmation rather than the broader concept of success, so the oracle stayed directly observable and not over-broad. The steps still exercised guest checkout and phone-sized execution, but Sarah's email receipt was excluded because that channel was not observable from this surface.

[self_critique] The negative case was present and specifically tied to the forbidden Sunday rule. I avoided over-broad validation messaging assertions because the source promised only that Sundays were not choosable, not how the UI explained that restriction.
